title: Transitland Atlas feed source evaluation
description: EXPERIMENTAL. Records why a feed URL was not registered in Atlas. One file per subject, named for its Onestop ID: an operator where one exists, otherwise a feed, since most feeds rely on generated operators. Holds current state, not an append-only log: git history is the log. Deliberately small. An earlier version carried a relationship vocabulary, a scope mechanism, per-candidate provenance and recheck scheduling; measured against 226 recorded candidates none of them changed any outcome, and each had to be explained and maintained, so they were removed.

operator_onestop_id.description: Operator this file is about. Must exist in feeds/. Use feed_onestop_id instead when the feed relies on a generated operator.

candidates.description: Feed URLs that have been evaluated and not registered.

feed_onestop_id.description: Feed this file is about, when the feed has no operator record. Must exist in feeds/.

us_ntd_id.description: US National Transit Database id, for an agency Atlas does not hold at all. Only valid when no operator carries this id: once one does, the file is renamed to that operator. Five characters, zero-padded, as NTD publishes them.

calitp_dataset_id.description: Cal-ITP dataset record id, for a California dataset Atlas does not hold. Their source of truth is an Airtable base surfaced through a warehouse, so these are `rec` plus fourteen characters and are stable for the life of the record. Used where NTD's id cannot be: that source publishes no identifier we can join on.

name.description: Human-readable name of the subject. Only useful on an externally-keyed file, where no Atlas record supplies one.

url.description: The URL evaluated. For a negative finding, the URL that does not work.

decision.description: not_used = works, but we chose something else. deferred = not now, expect to revisit. unavailable = cannot be used for reasons outside our control. All three suppress a discovery source identically; the distinction is for a human skimming the file. There is deliberately no `used` value, because the registry is what says a URL is in use.

relates_to.description: Registered feeds this decision was made against. More than one when a candidate spans several feeds.

decided_on.description: Date of the decision. Required, because every finding here decays.

rationale.description: Why, in plain terms, and briefly. Record what is expensive to rediscover, not the evidence trail: that a host is gone, that two builds differ structurally, that an agency asked for one feed over another. Anything cheap to re-measure belongs in the Transitland API instead. State the constraint that produced the decision, not only the decision -- a record that gives the verdict without the reason reads as settled and invites a wrong reversal, which has happened. Where the decision rests on something not examined, say so. State measurements rather than judgments about a vendor or agency: this repository is public.

references.description: Supporting links: agency pages, vendor directories, issues. Do not record PR numbers, which git history already resolves.
